title: Noah Lyles, Olympic 100-meter gold medalist, ends season early due to injury
content:
Noah Lyles, the American track star who won the 100-meter gold medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics, is ending his season early, one week before the new World Athletics Ultimate Championship.

In a social media video Friday, Lyles said he suffered a strain at the U.S. outdoor championships in June that led to other issues and his decision to shut it down ahead of the debut edition of track and field’s new biannual year-end showcase event.

“After running at USAs, we found out that I had a small strain, not very serious,” Lyles said, “and the rehab that we were putting together was going extremely well. Unfortunately, because of the strain, it caused some other things to flare up, and it’s made it hard for me to continue practicing. We decided that we’ll just end the season here, get ready for 2027, 2028, which are going to be humongous years.”

Those are the years of the next track and field world championships (Beijing, in 2027) and Olympics (Los Angeles, in 2028). Lyles has won five individual world titles to go along with his Olympic gold from Paris and has 13 medals total from his four world championships and two Olympic appearances.

Lyles said he will still attend next week’s Ultimate Championship in Budapest. It’s a new event featuring a select field of top athletes, meant to provide a showcase competition in the even years when there are no world championships.

“I still think that this is going to be an amazing competition,” Lyles said, “and I’m excited to watch that.”

The 29-year-old Lyles won gold in the 100 at Paris in a photo finish, narrowly edging out Jamaica’s Kishane Thompson and becoming the first American man to win the Olympic sprint since Justin Gatlin in 2004. He later took bronze in the 200 before collapsing on the track and being taken off in a wheelchair. He said he had tested positive for COVID-19 two days earlier.

A year later, Lyles won his fourth straight world title in the 200 but settled for bronze in the 100, behind Thompson and Jamaican countryman Oblique Seville.

Now, Lyles will set his sights on the build-up to the 2028 Games, starting with another world championship showdown next summer in Beijing.

“I’m even more excited (about) what the future’s going to bring,” Lyles said Friday. “This is reassurance that we’re going to kick 2027 off with a bang and give it our all.”
